record.paper_title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Existence of at least one good direction
record.original_question: In the same setting of a convex function f on a normed space and a fixed point x, is there at least one nonzero direction w for which the directional subdifferential limit lim_{t↓0} ∂f(x + t w) exists?

evidence.quote: Let us ask basic questions (see questions following (1) too): when does the limit in (3) exist? Is there any direction for which the limit exists?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a normed (real) vector space and let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous convex function. For each $y \in X$ let
$$\partial f(y) = \{ x^* \in X^* : f(z) \ge f(y) + \langle x^*, z - y\rangle \text{ for all } z \in X\}$$
denote the convex subdifferential of $f$ at $y$. Fix a point $x \in X$ and a nonzero direction $w \in X$. Say that the directional subdifferential limit
$$\lim_{t \downarrow 0} \partial f(x + t w)$$
exists (in the strong/norm sense) if there is a singleton $\{x^*\} \subset X^*$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $t_0 > 0$ with
$$\sup_{u^* \in \partial f(x + t w)} \|u^* - x^*\| < \varepsilon \quad \text{for all } 0 < t < t_0.$$

Question: Given any continuous convex function $f$ on a normed space $X$ and any point $x \in X$, does there always exist at least one nonzero direction $w \in X$ for which the above limit $\lim_{t \downarrow 0} \partial f(x + tw)$ exists?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on directional convergence of subgradients of convex functions. In finite-dimensional spaces, Rademacher's theorem yields a full-measure set of good directions, but in general infinite-dimensional normed spaces examples show that the set of "bad" directions can be a dense G_δ, and no general existence result for at least one good direction at every point appears to be known.

status_evidence.title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Directional convergence of subgradients of convex functions has been little explored... in the infinite-dimensional setting, it is hard to expect results of this form unless additional assumptions are imposed.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of directions along which subgradients converge is posed as an open question, particularly in infinite-dimensional normed spaces.

status_evidence.title: On the Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Companion work investigating directional strong convergence of subgradients.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats partial results but does not resolve the general existence of a good direction.
